argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only as a caveated certification. Aggregate readiness evidence and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall launch readiness, and public governance guidance supports decisions grounded in evaluation, monitoring, and documented risk management. But the same admissible record also shows a below-target developer-support migration slice, a model-card draft that does not yet reflect that limitation, and only a draft mitigation runbook with approval and threshold fields still TBD. Under the stated policy, that does not support clean certification without caveats. The supportable position is therefore to treat the certification decision as compliant only if it is explicitly qualified by disclosure of the unresolved API-migration support limitation unless and until an approved mitigation or risk acceptance is in place.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is necessary to defend the admissible position. This response does not rely on launch-velocity or partner-impact considerations as a basis to relax the policy threshold.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the controlling standard. Certification without material caveats requires either current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show either condition has been satisfied. The policy also requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless they are resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Draft monitoring and a draft runbook may support risk management, but they do not remove the present disclosure requirement.
concessions: Clean no-caveat certification is not supported by the current admissible record.
The draft mitigation runbook is not an approved mitigation under the policy because required approval/completeness elements remain missing.
The current model-card draft is not yet aligned with the admissible record if it continues to state there are no known material limitations.
